question: Compare U.S. comparable sales growth (ex-fuel where reported) for Walmart U.S. (Q2 FY2027), Costco U.S. (Q4 FY2026), and Target (Q2 2026), and explain why the periods aren't directly comparable.
grading: Key points: (1) each comp figure exact as disclosed with its adjustment basis stated; (2) states each period's end date and length (16 weeks for COST); (3) explains the misalignment and definitional differences; (4) no ranking conclusion that ignores the mismatch
answer: Walmart U.S. Q2 FY2027 comp sales grew 2.6% excluding fuel, for 13 weeks ended July 31, 2026. [G30-E1] Costco U.S. Q4 FY2026 comps grew 7.2% excluding gasoline-price and FX effects, for 16 weeks ended August 30, 2026 (headline U.S. comp growth was 10.7%). [G30-E2] Target Q2 2026 comparable sales grew 3.8% for 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026, under Target’s own store-and-digital definition; the release does not present a matching gas/FX-adjusted figure. [G30-E3] The quarters differ in length, end dates and adjustment definitions: Costco’s period is three weeks longer and includes more August trading. These figures therefore do not support a directly comparable market-share ranking.

output.answer:
Here is the comparison:

| Retailer | Period Reported | U.S. Comp Growth (Ex-Fuel) |
|----------|-----------------|----------------------------|
| **Walmart U.S.** | Q2 FY2027 (ended Jul 31, 2026) | **+2.6%** |
| **Costco U.S.** | Q4 FY2026 (ended Aug 30, 2026) | **+7.2%** (adjusted for gas/FX) |
| **Target** | Q2 2026 (ended Aug 1, 2026) | **+3.8%** |

*Sources: Walmart Q2 FY27 earnings ([corporate.walmart.com](https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2026/08/20/walmart-releases-q2-fy27-earnings), [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/104169/000010416926000145/earningsreleasefy27q2.htm)); Costco Q4 FY26 earnings ([investor.costco.com](https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2026-Operating-Results/default.aspx)); Target Q2 2026 earnings ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/08/target-corporation-reports-second-quarter-earnings))*

### Why the periods are not directly comparable

1. **Misaligned calendar windows**  
   Even though all three reports were released in August 2026, the periods they capture are different: Walmart ended July 31, Target ended August 1 and Costco ended August 30. Costco’s period captured an extra four weeks of late-summer and back-to-school demand that the other two did not.

2. **Different fiscal-quarter definitions**  
   Costco’s Q4 is a **16-week** quarter (its year-end), whereas standard retail quarters are **13 weeks**. A 23% longer period changes the base for growth calculations and smooths weekly volatility in ways the narrower windows for Walmart and Target do not.

3. **Different seasonal positioning**  
   Walmart and Target were both reporting mid-summer “Q2” results. Costco was reporting its fiscal Q4 (year-end), which has a different seasonal mix and typically includes heavier traffic ahead of the holiday and renewal cycle.

4. **Fuel-adjustment asymmetry**  
   Both Walmart and Costco explicitly strip out volatile gasoline sales when reporting “ex-fuel” figures. Target does not sell fuel in a material way, so its reported comp is inherently a different metric—there is no fuel impact to remove, making cross-company fuel-adjusted comparisons imprecise.

In short, the numbers reflect similar *calendar eras* (summer 2026), but they capture different slices of time, of different durations, in different seasonal contexts, and under slightly different calculation conventions.
